run.question: My signup service is failing and users can't register. What should I check to debug this issue?

report.summary: Observed facts: in namespace app-162 the Deployment payments-service and Deployment signup-service (both created 2026-11-21T03:37:16Z, revision 1, one ReplicaSet each) produced one payments pod and two signup pods at 03:37:16-03:37:17Z; all three pods are Running with restartCount 0 but Ready=False (ContainersNotReady), and both ClusterIP Services (payments-service:8080, signup-service:8080) have endpoint subsets with port 8080 but zero addresses. The payments-service container log states 'STRIPE_API_KEY is set to invalid test key - service will fail', logs 'Health check failed: Invalid Stripe API key' with /health and /ready returning 503, and the kubelet recorded 'Liveness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 503'. The Deployment takes STRIPE_API_KEY from Secret payments-secrets key stripe-api-key, and signup-service calls http://payments-service:8080 and logs 'Payments service check failed: <urlopen error [Errno 111] Connection refused>' with /ready 503 at 03:37:23, 03:37:28 and 03:37:33Z. So signup-service is itself failing its readiness check on its payments dependency and has no ready endpoints. The deepest object the evidence points at is Secret app-162/payments-secrets (the source of the invalid Stripe key), which I could not read; the signup -> payments failure chain is stated as the supported mechanism, while Prometheus and Jaeger were unavailable for this whole Run, so no error-rate, latency or trace evidence exists and user-facing registration errors were not directly observed. Conclusion is partial: no metrics/traces, no change history, secret value unread and no samples before 03:37:16Z.

claims.text: Namespace app-162 contains exactly two Deployments, payments-service (replicas 1) and signup-service (replicas 2), both created 2026-11-21T03:37:16Z; their status showed no readyReplicas/availableReplicas, and each has a single ReplicaSet of revision 1 created 2026-11-21T03:37:16Z (payments-service-6d94c44fdc, signup-service-7c89545dc9) with readyReplicas null.

All three app-162 pods (payments-service-6d94c44fdc-g5x7f, signup-service-7c89545dc9-8fdwb, signup-service-7c89545dc9-dth2h) are phase Running, created 2026-11-21T03:37:16Z with containers started 03:37:17Z, have restartCount 0 and container ready=false; their pod conditions show Ready=False and ContainersReady=False with reason ContainersNotReady ('containers with unready status: [<container>]').

payments-service container log lines (03:37:18.983-03:37:36.936Z) contain 'STRIPE_API_KEY is set to invalid test key - service will fail', 'GET /ready HTTP/1.1" 503', 'GET /health HTTP/1.1" 503' and twice 'Health check failed: Invalid Stripe API key'; no database error lines appear among the in-window lines read, and the container has no previous instance.

A Warning event on Pod app-162/payments-service-6d94c44fdc-g5x7f (reason Unhealthy, count 2, lastTimestamp 2026-11-21T03:37:36Z) records 'Liveness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 503'.

Deployment app-162/payments-service resolves STRIPE_API_KEY from secretKeyRef name payments-secrets key stripe-api-key (and DATABASE_URL from payments-secrets key database-url); Deployment app-162/signup-service sets PAYMENTS_SERVICE_URL=http://payments-service:8080 and resolves DATABASE_URL from secret signup-secrets key database-url. Both containers run image python:3.11-slim with readiness httpGet /ready:8080 and liveness httpGet /health:8080; signup liveness has initialDelaySeconds 30 and payments liveness failureThreshold 3 periodSeconds 10.

Both signup pods log readiness failures: 'Payments service check failed: <urlopen error [Errno 111] Connection refused>' followed by 'GET /ready HTTP/1.1" 503' at 03:37:23.160, 03:37:28.160 and 03:37:33.159-160Z; the signup containers have no previous instance and no other error lines in the window.

Service app-162/payments-service is ClusterIP port 8080 targetPort 8080 with selector app=payments-service, and its Endpoints object has port 8080 but an empty address list; Service app-162/signup-service is likewise port 8080 targetPort 8080 selector app=signup-service with an empty address list. The payments pod label is app=payments-service, matching the selector, and its containerPort is 8080.

In-window events for namespace app-162 are all Normal except one Unhealthy group: ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate x3 (signup-service-7c89545dc9 twice, payments-service-6d94c44fdc once), Deployment ScalingReplicaSet x2 ('Scaled up replica set signup-service-7c89545dc9 from 0 to 2' and 'payments-service-6d94c44fdc from 0 to 1'), plus Pod Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started; no OOMKilled, Evicted, Failed, BackOff or SuccessfulDelete reasons appear. The only ConfigMap in app-162 is kube-root-ca.crt.

The cluster's only fault/feature-flag source, ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config key demo.flagd.json, defines paymentFailure ('Fail payment service charge requests n%'), paymentUnreachable ('Payment service is unavailable') and other demo flags, and every flag's defaultVariant is 'off' (paymentFailure defaultVariant off, paymentUnreachable defaultVariant off); these flags target the otel-demo demo services, not app-162.

Mechanism hypothesis: the invalid stripe-api-key value delivered from Secret app-162/payments-secrets makes payments-service's /ready and /health return 503, so the payments pod never becomes Ready, Service payments-service has no endpoints and refuses connections, so signup-service's readiness probe to http://payments-service:8080 fails with 'Connection refused', both signup pods stay unready and Service signup-service has no endpoints - which is the plausible path by which registration requests cannot be served.

Second candidate still open: if the invalid key persists, payments-service liveness (failureThreshold 3, periodSeconds 10) will restart that container, and signup-service liveness only starts probing after 30s (initialDelaySeconds 30), so signup could additionally begin crash-looping shortly after this window. No restart or crashloop evidence exists inside the window (restartCount 0).

Rejected: OOMKilled / Evicted / CrashLoopBackOff as the cause. All three app-162 containers show restartCount 0 and state running with no lastState termination, no OOMKilled or Evicted events appear, and pods are phase Running without node pressure reasons.

Rejected: a switched-on fault-injection flag for payments. The only flag source (ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config) has paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable at defaultVariant 'off', and its flags address the otel-demo demo services rather than app-162 payments-service.

Rejected: a Service/port/selector misconfiguration between signup-service and payments-service. The payments Service selects app=payments-service (the pod's label), targetPort 8080 equals the container port 8080, and the Endpoints object exists with port 8080 but no addresses - the emptiness follows the unready pods, not a label or port mismatch.

Deployment 'payment' in namespace otel-demo is a different entity from app-162/payments-service and reported 1 ready / 1 available replica; it is not the URL signup-service calls, so its status says nothing about the app-162 dependency. Its application logs were not examined.

Namespace app-100a holds separate workloads (loki, payment-api-100a) whose pods are Running with ready containers and restartCount 0; signup-service's configured dependency is http://payments-service:8080 in app-162, so these app-100a objects are a different entity and were not tied to this failure.

Check first (in this order): (1) Secret app-162/payments-secrets key stripe-api-key - the payments-service log states the key is invalid; correct it and re-check payments-service /ready and /health, (2) Pod app-162/payments-service-6d94c44fdc-g5x7f logs and its readiness/liveness probe results, (3) Deployment app-162/signup-service pod logs for the payments check, and Service/Endpoints app-162/payments-service and app-162/signup-service address lists, (4) events in app-162 for probe failures. All of these were inspected here with the Kubernetes tools; do not edit anything without authorization.

After the key is corrected, verify the chain end to end: payments-service /ready 200 -> payments Endpoints gains an address -> signup pods become Ready -> signup Endpoints gains addresses; and consider whether signup-service should treat a payments outage as a hard readiness failure, since that makes registration unavailable whenever the dependency is unready.

gaps: Secret values cannot be read: the actual value of Secret app-162/payments-secrets key stripe-api-key was not verified; its invalidity is reported only by the payments-service container log.

The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so when and by whom the stripe-api-key value or the app-162 objects (both Deployments created 2026-11-21T03:37:16Z) were changed is unknown.

Prometheus was unavailable for the whole Run (get_label_values, get_metric_names, execute_prometheus_instant_query, metrics_range_query, list_prometheus_rules all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no error-rate or latency series were obtained; signup/payments ERROR series and request rates are unknown, not zero.

Jaeger was unavailable for the whole Run (traces_list_services, traces_search for frontend, traces_list_operations for payment all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no span-level evidence exists; no complete call chain can be claimed and the listed available services do not include signup-service or app-162 payments-service.

No samples exist before 2026-11-21T03:37:16Z for these workloads - both Deployments, ReplicaSets and pods were created then - so whether signup was already failing earlier in the 24h window is unknown.

User-facing registration failures were not directly observed: no ingress objects were returned by the query (status no_data) and no frontend/load-generator logs were examined; 'users can't register' is consistent with both Services having empty endpoint lists, but no request-level error was seen.
Cluster-wide networkpolicies and resourcequotas queries returned no objects with status no_data, so a network policy or quota contribution could neither be confirmed nor excluded from those results.
The fault-injection flag values in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config were read at query time (now), not at the time of the incident, and only one flag source is visible.

signup-service's own DATABASE_URL dependency (Secret signup-secrets key database-url) could not be verified; no database error lines appeared in the in-window signup log lines read, which is not proof of database health.
next_steps: A human with secret-read rights should confirm whether app-162/payments-secrets key stripe-api-key holds a valid test Stripe key and correct it if not.

Once corrected, restart/roll the payments-service workload and confirm its /ready endpoint returns 200 and that Service payments-service gains an endpoint address; then confirm both signup pods become Ready.
Enable the Prometheus and Jaeger integrations for this target so error-rate, latency and trace evidence can be used, and enable change history to date any secret or workload change.
